summary: Open 3D membrane-segmented time series that begin at or before the four-cell stage exist for the mouse (Zenodo 13903500, CC BY, one embryo) and the ascidian Phallusia (figshare project 64301 and Zenodo mirrors, ASTEC segmentation of 19 articles), so contacts and any four-way junction can in principle be read from label images. No frog, sea-urchin, mollusc or annelid volume was found, Xenbase and Echinobase returned HTTP 429, and none of the sets flags 'full fluid contact', which is the claim's condition.
next_step: Open the Phallusia and mouse label images at the four-cell timepoint to confirm they are present, and define the contact criterion (minimum shared area) and a 'fluid contact' proxy before scoring; retry Xenbase/Echinobase later for frog and urchin images.
obstacles_confirmed: Mouse and ascidian embryos are the only species with open segmented volumes found; classical frog, urchin, mollusc and annelid material was not located.
Full-fluid-contact condition is not annotated in any dataset.
